summary: Regulators finalized a rule Wednesday that would slash payments for drugs in the controversial 340B program and equalize some payments between care sites. Hospitals railed against the rule.
title: Medicare will cut billions from 340B, expand site-neutral payments in 2027

summary: Siemens Healthineers said Thursday it will rebrand its in vitro diagnostics business and establish the unit as a standalone organization by mid-2028. The rebranded business, Olyrian Diagnostics, will sell diagnostics for laboratory and point-of-care testing. Clients include Quest Diagnostics, which recently extended its contract by five years. Siemens Healthineers is rebranding its remaining business. Next year, the company will start a three-year transition to rebrand as Healthineers, dropping Siemens from its name. The rebrand coincides with a plan announced late last year for Siemens to give up its controlling stake in Siemens Healthineers. Shareholders will vote about the plan to spin off Siemens Healthineers shares at an annual meeting in February.
title: Siemens Healthineers to rebrand and separate its IVD business

summary: Going forward, the heart valve maker expects procedure volumes to rise following positive study data and expanded Medicare reimbursement.
title: Edwards bumps up sales forecast on TAVR strength in Q3

summary: Boston Scientific has formed an alliance with Blackstone Life Sciences to co-fund development of its Vitalyst miniature heart pump. Blackstone, which disclosed the agreement Monday, will provide up to $455 million in return for potential regulatory and commercial milestone payments, plus royalties on net sales. Boston Scientific focused on developing Vitalyst in acute myocardial infarction cardiogenic shock following setbacks to Johnson & Johnson’s rival Impella pump in another indication.
title: Boston Scientific, Blackstone agree to $455M deal to co-fund heart pump development

summary: Segal is succeeding Robert Vigersky, who is transitioning to a chief medical officer emeritus role ahead of his planned retirement at the end of next year.
title: MiniMed names David Segal chief medical officer

summary: CEO Ivan Tornos did not attribute the company’s performance in knees to a broader market slowdown, as competitor Stryker did last week.
title: Zimmer raises sales forecast despite slower knee business

summary: Philips reached an agreement with the Department of Justice to pay 288 million euros (about $322 million) to settle criminal and civil investigations related to its recall of millions of sleep and respiratory devices, the company disclosed Tuesday. Philips began the recall of more than 15 million devices in 2021 after finding soundproofing foam could break down and be inhaled by users. The recall included continuous positive airway pressure and bilevel positive airway pressure machines, as well as ventilators. The settlement is separate from a consent decree the Food and Drug Administration struck with Philips in 2024, which has barred the sale of certain respiratory devices in the U.S. until Philips meets requirements set out by the agency.
title: Philips settles with DOJ over recalled CPAP machines

summary: Edwards’ TAVR results in moderate aortic stenosis drew applause from meeting attendees, while Medtronic’s renal denervation and Abbott’s left atrial appendage closure devices also produced positive study findings.
